commenti.body:
At his best (and the Monica Vitti B&W trilogy is, for my money, some of the best of all time), Antonioni is focused on delivering a scathing critique of the Italian bourgeoisie and the “modernity” of the 20th century Western world that allowed such a class to exist. 

For me, those movies are about the impossibility of love in “modern” times, when the meaning of self/society/other/even words like love had been displaced and replaced in one swift motion - so as not to be noticed - with a hollow façade concerned more with the image, the material, or the appearance rather than what lies behind it. I think these films serve to call that out and interrogate it, and what I love most about them is they never posit solutions (only hopelessness lol).

Anyways, it’s late and I am tired and starting to get hyperbolic so I’m sorry, but I love Antonioni and could talk about his films for hours. So much to dig into
No, I think you're exactly right. The romantic ideals have been replaced with more hedonistic pursuits, whether that be money, sex, or materialism.
